page: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is an x86_64 cloud server instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores using simultaneous multithreading (two threads per core). It is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Vector processing is supported through AVX-512 instructions, including VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server includes 5670 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, contains no discrete GPUs, and operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results demonstrate high throughput across compute, data manipulation, and web workloads. In CPU stress testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 175877.61 and a single-core score of 3725.27, placing it in the top tier of tested servers. Memory bandwidth reaches 173.94 GB/sec for uncached writes and 309.38 GB/sec for uncached reads. Data processing tests show bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speeds of 599.98 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 41.15 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks recorded 139.48 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 38180.79, and static web serving throughput of 93.44 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory distribution offers strong compute and local I/O resource density without the expense of surplus RAM capacity. The integrated 5670 GB NVMe storage provides high-speed scratch space for disk-intensive batch tasks without requiring supplementary remote block storage. However, memory-intensive workloads requiring large memory-to-core footprints and tasks needing dedicated GPU acceleration are constrained by the 192.0 GB ceiling and the absence of accelerator hardware. Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is best aligned with parallel compilation, batch data compression, in-memory caching systems, high-concurrency web serving, and database tasks requiring fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is a compute-focused instance featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The platform includes 192.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, without discrete graphics acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for raw compute and I/O tasks, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 175877.61, static web serving throughput of 93.44 GB/sec, and 139.48 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware support includes AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and VAES encryption instructions. Given its lower RAM-to-CPU ratio and large NVMe disk pool, it is well suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, batch data compression, caching infrastructure, and local scratch-space database systems.
